currency_note: weekly_base is measured in billions of MD dollars per week, as a gameplay budget abstraction, not a literal historical account. Runtime applies the approved civil/development/security/self-government multipliers; no annual amount is stored.

administrations.name: British Caribbean Colonies
administrations.notes: Small eastern Caribbean dependencies. Distinct from the self-governing Bahamas and British Honduras; direct colonial government in 1970.

administrations.name: Bahamas
administrations.notes: Internal self-government since 1964; still a UK colony on 1970-01-01. Treat as a peaceful transition administration, not as a centrally governed colony.

administrations.name: British Honduras
administrations.notes: Self-government within the colony and an active Guatemalan sovereignty claim; independence negotiations remain unresolved. No armed independence war in 1970.

administrations.name: Hong Kong
administrations.notes: Crown colony with appointed executive and limited elected representation; do not infer sovereignty from adjacent Chinese cores. An independently controlled HKG native successor ends administration; a still-subject HKG remains associated with its actual overlord.

administrations.name: Gibraltar
administrations.notes: British colony with local self-government; sovereignty dispute with Spain, including the 1967 referendum. Low internal resistance, external diplomatic contest.

administrations.name: British Atlantic Dependencies
administrations.notes: Bermuda, Falklands, South Georgia, Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha. Sparse populations and varied constitutional arrangements; grouped for scale.

administrations.name: British Solomon Islands Protectorate
administrations.notes: The two map states represent the protectorate: Solomon Islands (533) and Guadalcanal (1225). Their province lists do not overlap. Political mobilization is present, but no 1970 anti-colonial war.

administrations.name: Gilbert and Ellice Islands Colony
administrations.notes: Grouped as the single Gilbert and Ellice Islands colonial administration; map splits Gilbert, Ellice/Tuvalu, Line and Phoenix island groups. Sparse and locally administered.

administrations.name: Fiji
administrations.notes: Still a British colony on 1970-01-01, with internal self-government and independence scheduled for 10 October 1970. Remove after independence if runtime dates forward.

administrations.name: Seychelles
administrations.notes: A UK colony with an elected Governing Council under the 1967 constitution; political parties differed over independence, and a 1970 constitutional conference was planned. The main parties' peaceful constitutional competition warrants associated/low resistance treatment, not a war profile.

administrations.name: New Hebrides Condominium
administrations.notes: Anglo-French condominium; map owner is ENG, so any runtime logic must preserve joint French administration as a diplomatic/controller nuance rather than silently treating it as ordinary UK colony.

administrations.name: Tokelau
administrations.notes: New Zealand-administered non-self-governing territory; keep separate from the self-governing Cook Islands and Niue.

administrations.name: Cook Islands
administrations.notes: Self-governing in free association with New Zealand since 1965. This is not ordinary colonial administration; preserve its autonomy.

administrations.name: French Overseas Territories
administrations.notes: French Polynesia, Kerguelen/French Southern Lands, New Caledonia and Wallis and Futuna. Kerguelen is uninhabited and runtime should suppress resistance/support in state 70; French Polynesia and New Caledonia have distinct local political institutions.

administrations.name: Comoros
administrations.notes: Autonomous overseas territory; Mayotte and Anjouan are separate map states. Preserve island-level political variation; the archipelago is not yet independent in 1970.

administrations.name: French Somaliland
administrations.notes: Territory of the Afars and Issas; states 230 and 1020 jointly represent the French-administered territory. Local political dispute is growing; no ongoing independence war in January 1970.

administrations.name: French Overseas Departments
administrations.notes: Réunion, French Guiana, Guadeloupe and Martinique were overseas departments/integral parts of France, not colonial possessions. Included only as associated administrative coverage; omit from any colony-only resistance or independence mechanic.

administrations.name: Angola
administrations.notes: Portuguese colonial war ongoing since 1961; three competing liberation movements and active armed conflict. State list reflects actual January 1970 POR ownership.

administrations.name: Mozambique
administrations.notes: FRELIMO armed struggle began in 1964 and remained active in 1970, especially in the north. States 1049/1050 are dated Portuguese-owned Niassa districts; confirm map grouping before runtime use.

administrations.name: Portuguese Guinea
administrations.notes: PAIGC independence war was active and had established liberated zones; Portuguese authority was contested across much of the territory. Both listed map states are POR-owned in 1970.

administrations.name: Suriname
administrations.notes: Autonomous constituent country within the Kingdom of the Netherlands, with internal self-government under the 1954 Charter; independence came in 1975. Map splits coastal and Sipaliwini regions.

administrations.name: Netherlands Antilles
administrations.notes: Self-governing country within the Kingdom under the 1954 Charter, not an ordinary colony. State 49 represents the Antilles group; do not split individual island administrations absent map representation.

administrations.name: Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands
administrations.notes: UN strategic trust territory, administered by the United States. State 818 mixes Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands, both represented in the separate associated row because the map cannot split them; states 819–821 represent Palau, the Marshall Islands and the Caroline Islands. Runtime recognises separately independent Palau, Marshall Islands and Micronesia through their actual native MD core tags, so one successor does not become a new colonial administrator.

administrations.name: Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands
administrations.notes: The state combines Guam (US territory with local civil government) and the Northern Mariana Islands (part of the US Trust Territory). Both were under US administration in 1970, so the merged state may be represented as a quiet/associated administration; do not treat it as a war or falsely remove it from the Trust Territory.

administrations.name: American Samoa
administrations.notes: Unincorporated US territory with a distinct local political status; not part of the Pacific Trust Territory.

administrations.name: United States Virgin Islands
administrations.notes: US territory with local elected government; include as associated administration, not an active insurgency.

administrations.name: Puerto Rico
administrations.notes: Commonwealth/free associated state since 1952, with elected government and internal self-government. It is not a conventional colony; never apply ordinary colonial control penalties.

administrations.name: Australian-administered Papua and New Guinea (partial map coverage)
administrations.notes: Australia historically administered Papua and the UN Trust Territory of New Guinea, but the 1970 dated map confirms Australian ownership only of Bismarck Archipelago (733) and Bougainville (941). Mainland Papua/New Guinea states are not Australian-owned in dated history and PAP has no confirmed 1970 world-setup puppet relationship in the inspected project files. Preserve this discrepancy explicitly; do not treat PAP as independent by inference or silently correct ownership. PAP is also an imprecise single native tag because these states have PAP/SOL cores.

administrations.name: South West Africa (Namibia)
administrations.notes: South Africa continued its administration despite UN termination of the mandate; UN Security Council Resolution 276 (1970) declared its continued presence illegal. SWAPO insurgency began in 1966, with armed operations from Zambia from 1968. Preserve disputed/illegal administration status; this is not a normal South African province.

administrations.name: Spanish Sahara
administrations.notes: Spanish-administered territory; anti-Spanish demonstrations in El Aaiun occurred in 1970 and the Zemla uprising was repressed; organised Polisario war had not yet begun. Use contested, not war, for a January 1970 start. Tifariti and Western Sahara are the mod's two states.

administrations.name: Greenland
administrations.notes: A Danish county with limited local government at the start of 1970; home rule came in 1979. The dated map's states are owned by DEN and core GRN. Preserve the political trend toward autonomy without framing it as armed colonial resistance.

administrations.name: Faroe Islands
administrations.notes: Self-governing Danish territory under Home Rule since 1948, with a distinct Faroese government and parliament; not a conventional colony.

administrations.name: Brunei Protected State
administrations.notes: A protected sovereign state: UK responsible for external affairs and security consultation under treaty, while the Sultanate retained local authority. Country-level diplomatic protection only: the listed state is locally owned, not ENG-owned. Require the live ENG subject relationship; do not transfer territory or create colonial resistance. In 1970 the Legislative Council was prorogued and elections suspended, but this was not a war.

administrations.name: Bahrain Protected State
administrations.notes: British treaty protection until independence in August 1971; it was a sovereign sheikhdom, not UK-owned territory. Apply only to a live British protector relationship, with no state ownership or transfer.

administrations.name: Qatar Protected State
administrations.notes: British treaty protection until independence in September 1971; Qatar was a sovereign sheikhdom, not UK-owned territory. Apply only to a live British protector relationship, with no state ownership or transfer.

administrations.name: Trucial States Protection
administrations.notes: The seven Trucial sheikhdoms were individually protected sovereigns, not UK-owned land; the scenario retains the UAE tag for their union. States 179 (Dubai) and 180 (Abu Dhabi) are UAE-owned/controller-controlled anchors. Require a live ENG subject relationship; never transfer these states or create armed resistance. The protection relationship ends with the 1971 withdrawal.

administrations.name: Cape Verde
administrations.notes: Portuguese colony in 1970; the anti-colonial war did not spread here. Amilcar Cabral led the PAIGC for both Guinea-Bissau and Cape Verde, but no Cabo Verde front was being fought. Keep separate from Portuguese Guinea because its status and wartime exposure differed.

administrations.name: São Tomé and Príncipe
administrations.notes: Portuguese island territory with no active liberation war in 1970. Its later independence should not remove Macau or Timor administration.

administrations.name: Macau
administrations.notes: Portuguese-administered enclave with a distinct local administration and historical Sino-Portuguese settlement; no 1970 liberation war. Keep its administration independent from other Portuguese colonies in runtime.

administrations.name: Portuguese Timor
administrations.notes: Portuguese administration of East Timor. The map splits it between Loro Munu and Timor Leste; both are POR-owned in dated history, and their province lists do not overlap.

administrations.name: Pitcairn Islands
administrations.notes: Tiny Pacific colony with a very small population; keep its recurring cost negligible.

administrations.name: Tonga Protected State
administrations.notes: Tonga was an independent sovereign kingdom under British protection at the start of 1970; the protection treaty ended on 4 June 1970. State 1115 is TON-owned/controller-controlled. Apply only while a live ENG subject/protector relationship remains, with no ownership transfer or armed resistance.

administrations.name: Niue
administrations.notes: Administered by New Zealand through a resident commissioner in 1970. Niue was offered autonomy in 1965 but did not accept at that time; self-government in free association began on 19 October 1974. Do not model as already associated in January 1970.

administrations.name: Saint-Pierre and Miquelon
administrations.notes: French overseas territory (territoire d’outre-mer, TOM) in 1970; it became an overseas department only in 1976. Keep it separate from the French overseas departments and charge only a tiny quiet administration cost.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Isle of Man and Channel Islands
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Crown dependencies with distinct self-governing constitutional status, not colonies; do not add to colonial control mechanics.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Christmas and Cocos Islands
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Australian external territories, but no representative native administration/independence movement was identified; defer rather than impose a colonial resistance system.

excluded_or_deferred.name: South Africa proper
excluded_or_deferred.reason: The colonial target is Namibia only; do not treat apartheid's internal racial order as foreign colonial administration for this registry.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Réunion/French Guiana/Guadeloupe/Martinique
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Already included as associated departments to record jurisdiction, but excluded from colonial resistance/independence mechanics. Saint-Pierre and Miquelon was still a TOM and is a separate quiet row.

excluded_or_deferred.name: French Kerguelen
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Uninhabited French Southern and Antarctic Lands component; no native population to administer.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Okinawa
excluded_or_deferred.reason: US military occupation/administration pending reversion to Japan in 1972; different legal and political process from colonial affairs.

excluded_or_deferred.name: British Sovereign Base Areas in Cyprus
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Military bases on Cypriot territory, not a British colony; do not add routine colonial administration costs or resistance.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Spanish Ceuta, Melilla, Canary Islands and metropolitan Spain
excluded_or_deferred.reason: The Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla were Spanish territory, not the Spanish Sahara colony. Metropolitan Spanish states and enclaves are excluded from colonial administration.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Portuguese Azores and Madeira
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Portuguese autonomous/administrative island districts integrated into the state, not colonies.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Hawaii and Attu Island
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Hawaii was a US state and Attu is a sparsely inhabited strategic island; neither is a 1970 colonial administration.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Norfolk Island
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Australian external territory with local administration; not a representative colonial/armed independence case for this mechanic.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Guantanamo Bay, Midway, Wake, Johnston and Diego Garcia
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Strategic military enclaves or sparsely inhabited possessions, not local colonial administrations. Diego Garcia (state 824) is UK sovereignty in 1970 despite the mod's USA owner/controller representation; exclude pending a separate Chagos/BIOT ownership audit.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Papua New Guinea mainland
excluded_or_deferred.reason: Although Australia historically administered Papua and the UN Trust Territory of New Guinea, the 1970 scenario includes PAP as a country and country-level subject/puppet relations must decide administration coverage. The state map dates 730–732 away from Australia. Do not infer or fix ownership from cores; use PAP subject status if present and keep this issue explicit.

excluded_or_deferred.name: Brunei, Qatar, Bahrain and Gulf protectorates
excluded_or_deferred.reason: These country-level British protector relationships are represented by locally owned state anchors with subject_only=true and are included as associated rows in administrations. Runtime must require the actual ENG subject relationship; it must not transfer these states. Tonga is likewise included separately and its protection expires in June 1970. Oman is independent, not a formal British protectorate.
